description: The explicit DISPLAY scope terminator END-DISPLAY (ISO 14.9.11.2) - a COBOL-2002 introduction, with END-ACCEPT. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): the ANSI X3.23-1985 format is `DISPLAY { identifier-1 | literal-1 } … [ UPON mnemonic-name-1 ] [ WITH NO ADVANCING ]` (§1985:VI.6.10.2), with no terminator, and §1985:IV.4.4.4 'The explicit scope terminators are the following' lists nineteen (END-ADD through END-WRITE) without END-DISPLAY; §2002:14.8.10.1 Format 1 prints `[ UPON mnemonic-name-1 ] [ WITH NO ADVANCING ] [ END-DISPLAY ]`, and §2002:14.4 Table 13 pairs `DISPLAY | [NOT] ON EXCEPTION | END-DISPLAY`, the conditional phrase of the screen DISPLAY 2002 adds (§2002:F.2 item 45: 'The DISPLAY statement is extended to allow a screen item specified in the screen section to be used for output to the operator of a terminal'). §2014:14.9.10.1 prints the 2002 format unchanged, so 2014 = 2023. The registered end-accept twin had a gate and END-DISPLAY had NONE, so `DISPLAY X END-DISPLAY` was silently accepted at 85 (kb/Work PB134).
